title: 1000 Cuts
subtitle: A dated chronology of the Williams family's position at Great House Farm in law and in fact, 1870s to 1988, each step linked to its evidence

peak.event: John Williams holds Great House Farm from the Bute estate; a Feb 1916 Bute yearly tenancy with plan names him; the 1904 Bute rent audit lists him "of Llandough Farm".
peak.label: Record
peak.changed: On paper, the occupation is a tenancy from the Bute estate: the 1904 rent audit [EV-0227] and the Feb 1916 tenancy with plan [EV-0014] both name John Williams as tenant.

peak.event: Marconi's wireless tests at Lavernock and Flat Holm, close by. Family tradition holds that he stayed at the farm.
peak.label: Not yet confirmed
peak.changed: The 1897 press and the extracts of Kemp's diary record the tests at Lavernock and Flat Holm [EV-0011] [EV-0248] [EV-0256]; none of the extracts read so far names Great House Farm.
peak.open: Did the Marconi team stay at the farm? The full Kemp diary (Bodleian MS. Marconi 89) or a letter placing the team there would answer it.

peak.event: "Peerless" Jim Driscoll's first fight in the farm barn.
peak.label: Not yet confirmed
peak.changed: A local-history summary places the fight in the farm barn [EV-0009]; the year and the National Monuments Record citation have not been located.
peak.open: When was the fight, and what is the primary source? A dated report or the NMR entry would answer it.

peak.event: Trees planted on Parcel A, the house parcel, in view of the town: one of the family's acts of occupation.
peak.label: Family testimony
peak.changed: The family's account of tree planting on Parcel A, with an undated photograph [EV-0009] [EV-0199].
peak.open: What did the planting cover, and when? Dated photographs, aerial images or survey sheets would answer it.

peak.event: Last rent for the house parcel paid in 1928, when the quarry machinery left; no rent for the house parcel after that.
peak.label: Family testimony
peak.changed: The family's account [EV-0016]; no receipt for 1928 has been located. The Court of Appeal recorded rent arrears in the mid-1930s and late 1940s and a last payment, under a judgment for arrears, in 1953 [EV-0080].
peak.open: Which is right for the house parcel: rent ending in 1928, or arrears and a 1953 payment? A rent book or the 1953 judgment file would answer it.

peak.event: No one takes issue with the stopped rent for about twenty years, until the 1949 surrender and re-grant (family account).
peak.label: Family testimony
peak.changed: The family's account [EV-0016]. The judgment gives arrears "in the mid-1930s and in the late 1940s" as the background to the 1949 arrangement [EV-0025] [EV-0080].

peak.event: The 1939 Western Ground Rents agreement plan shows the fields (Parcel B) only, highlighted; the house parcel is not shown on it.
peak.label: Record
peak.changed: The plan to the 1939 Western Ground Rents agreement highlights the fields (Parcel B) and does not show the house parcel [EV-0023]. Page 1 of the agreement is not yet held.
peak.open: What does page 1 of the 1939 agreement describe as let?

cuts.event: Bute grants John Williams a yearly agricultural tenancy of "the whole of the farm", with plan.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The family's occupation is put in writing as a yearly agricultural tenancy of "the whole of the farm" [EV-0014]. The Court of Appeal opens its account of the facts with this letting [EV-0080].

cuts.event: Bute (Mountjoy) sells the reversion to Western Ground Rents Ltd, a ground-rent company; the conveyance later becomes the root of title.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The reversion passes from the Bute estate to Western Ground Rents Ltd [EV-0019] [EV-0022]; this conveyance later serves as the root of title in the chain that leads to BP [EV-0216].
cuts.open: Was the farmhouse parcel inside the 1938 conveyance and plan? The conveyance and plan would answer it.

cuts.event: The Limitation Act 1939 comes into force: 12 years of adverse possession bars the owner (s.10 possession must be "adverse"; s.13 a formal entry alone keeps nothing alive).
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: From 1 July 1940, 12 years of adverse possession bars the owner's claim (s.10 requires the possession to be "adverse"; under s.13 a formal entry alone does not stop the clock). The 1987 judgment applies this Act to every later step [EV-0080].

cuts.event: The courts record John Williams as falling into rent arrears.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The courts treat the unpaid rent as arrears under a continuing tenancy, not as the end of the tenancy [EV-0080]. The family's account dates the end of rent to 1928 [EV-0016].

cuts.event: John Williams's tenancy is surrendered and a new yearly agricultural tenancy is granted to his son-in-law Frederick Buckler. It is never put in writing.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The tenancy passes from John Williams to Frederick Buckler as a new yearly tenancy, never put in writing [EV-0025] [EV-0080]. The occupier is now a tenant of the 1949 grant.
cuts.open: Why was the 1949 re-grant made, and on whose initiative? Estate correspondence from 1948–49 would answer it.

cuts.event: Family title papers removed from the farmhouse blanket box.
cuts.label: Family testimony
cuts.changed: The family's account: the title papers kept in the farmhouse blanket box were removed [EV-0026]. No court record mentions them.
cuts.open: What were the papers, and where are they now?

cuts.event: Frederick Buckler's last rent payment, made under a county-court judgment for arrears.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: A rent payment made under a county-court judgment for arrears [EV-0080] [EV-0030]. In law a payment of rent acknowledges the landlord's title, so no 12-year period runs before it.

cuts.event: A further attempt to treat Frederick Buckler as a tenant.
cuts.label: Not yet confirmed
cuts.changed: A further step treating Frederick Buckler as a tenant is listed in the family record [EV-0031]; its source has not been located.
cuts.open: What happened in 1954? The source document would answer it.

cuts.event: A notice to quit ends Frederick Buckler's tenancy.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The tenancy ends; Frederick Buckler stays on without one. The Court of Appeal held that Frederick and Mary were in adverse possession of the house and garden from this date [EV-0080].

cuts.event: Western Ground Rents obtains a summary possession order (Order 14) in the High Court and enforces it on 4 July 1955: all the farm is taken except the farmhouse and garden.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The High Court order is enforced on 4 July 1955 and every part of the farm except the farmhouse and garden is taken into possession [EV-0032] [EV-0034] [EV-0080]. The family records that Mary had just had a leg amputated and refused to leave [EV-0034]. The order itself is not yet located.
cuts.open: What exactly did the 1955 order cover? The High Court order would answer it.

cuts.event: Leckwith Common inquiry and Glamorgan County Council acquisitions near the farm; Mary's "Crichel Down" objection goes no further, and no petition is presented in Parliament.
cuts.label: Record (press)
cuts.changed: Land near the farm passes into public schemes after the Leckwith Common inquiry [EV-0035] [EV-0036]. Mary's "Crichel Down" objection is recorded [EV-0037]; no petition was presented in Parliament [EV-0038].
cuts.open: What became of the 1958 objection? The inquiry file would answer it.

cuts.event: Western Ground Rents offers Mary a tenancy of the house and garden; she refuses. Alternative housing is offered and refused.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: Tenancy and housing offers are made and refused [EV-0039]. In 1986 the trial judge relied on the March 1965 offer in finding that Frederick had no intention to possess as owner [EV-0080].

cuts.event: Cardiff County Court possession order for the farmhouse and garden (Judge Temple Morris QC), with mesne profits; a suspended committal order against Frederick Buckler follows in June 1963.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: A court orders possession of the farmhouse and garden [EV-0041] [EV-0030]. The Court of Appeal held that this order stopped the 12-year period before it had run, so the owner's title was not extinguished [EV-0080]. The order was not enforced until leave was sought in 1974.

cuts.event: Frederick Buckler dies. Mary stays in the house.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: Mary remains the occupier. The trial judge held that, while Frederick lived, only his intention counted [EV-0080].

cuts.event: Western Ground Rents sells the farm, including the farmhouse, to BP Pension Trust.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The paper title, and as successor the benefit of the 1962 order, passes to BP Pension Trust [EV-0043] [EV-0080].

cuts.event: Village green VG41 registered by Glamorgan County Council.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: A village green, VG41, is registered by the county council [EV-0044]. The certified map shows a small roadside wedge [EV-0263].
cuts.open: Does VG41 overlap the house parcel? An overlay of the certified map on the 1916 plan would answer it.

cuts.event: Outline planning permission for about 13 houses, with an ownership certificate.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: Outline permission for about 13 houses is granted on an application carrying an ownership certificate [EV-0046]. The site is now on the planning register as a development site.
cuts.open: Who signed the 1972 ownership certificate, and was the occupier notified? The planning file would answer it.

cuts.event: BP Pension Trust's new possession action: Mary pleads that BP's claim is barred by adverse possession under the 1939 Act. The action is adjourned part-heard and "has never been finally heard".
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: Mary pleads that BP's claim is barred by adverse possession under the 1939 Act. The action is adjourned part-heard and, in the Court of Appeal's words, "has never been finally heard" [EV-0049] [EV-0080]. No decision on that plea is on the record.
cuts.open: What does the 1974 court file show was pleaded and left undecided? The HMCTS reply due 2 Nov 2026 would answer it.

cuts.event: BP Pension Trust gets leave to execute the 1962 order (Judge Watkin Powell); the warrant may be enforced from 31 Oct 1974. She appeals, saying she had too little notice to be heard.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: Leave is given to execute the 1962 order, enforceable from 31 Oct 1974 [EV-0041] [EV-0080]; the 12-year period from that order would have ended on 11 Dec 1974. Her appeal raised too little notice to be heard.

cuts.event: Two letters, from BP Pension Trust and BP Properties, sent to her solicitor, allow her to stay rent-free for life: "no proceedings will be commenced until you personally no longer live there".
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The letters permit her to stay rent-free for life [EV-0050] [EV-0048]. The Court of Appeal held that from then on her possession was "by the licence of BP Properties" and no longer adverse [EV-0080].

cuts.event: On her solicitors' advice she does nothing while the 12 years from the 1962 order run out, and does not reject the letters.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The Court of Appeal recorded that she did not reject the letters: "she did not, however, do that" [EV-0080] [EV-0050]. The court treated that as accepting the licence.
cuts.open: Did Mary or her solicitors write after 31 Oct 1974 rejecting the licence? Such a letter would meet the point the Court of Appeal identified.

cuts.event: BP Pension Trust conveys the farmhouse plot and other land to BP Properties, reserving 80-year road and sewer rights "to serve any development".
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The farmhouse plot passes from BP Pension Trust to BP Properties, with 80-year road and sewer rights reserved "to serve any development" [EV-0052].

cuts.event: The Vale of Glamorgan becomes a compulsory registration area.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: First registration becomes compulsory on sale in the Vale of Glamorgan [EV-0265].

cuts.event: The fields (Parcel B) pass between BP companies and are registered (WA231076), as the law required within two months.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The fields (Parcel B) pass between BP companies and are registered as WA231076 [EV-0059] [EV-0071]. After this the farmhouse is the only unregistered part of the BP holding at the farm.

cuts.event: BP Properties applies to register the farmhouse (Form 1C, WA240304) while Mary is alive.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: BP Properties applies to register the farmhouse, WA240304, on Form 1C, while Mary is alive and living there [EV-0066] [EV-0063]. The form requires the applicant to state that it is in possession [EV-0065].
cuts.open: What did BP state about possession and the occupier? The application papers would answer it.

cuts.event: Mary Williams (Mrs Buckler) dies, after an illness in the weeks before (family testimony).
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: Mary Williams (Mrs Buckler) dies [EV-0067]; the family records an illness in the weeks before. BP's 1974 undertaking ran "until you personally no longer live there" [EV-0050]; in 1988 BP's spokesman gave her death as the point when "it became clear her son was not going to leave" [EV-0088].

cuts.event: The Registry examines the farmhouse application after her death: Linklaters letter of 8 Apr (form D23), correspondence of 12 Apr and letters of 12 May 1983.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The Registry examines the application after her death: Linklaters' letter of 8 Apr (form D23), correspondence of 12 Apr and letters of 12 May 1983 [EV-0069] [EV-0070] [EV-0071]. The title takes effect from the application date.
cuts.open: What did the 1983 letters tell the Registry about who lived in the house? The Registry copy file, due 28 Oct 2026, would answer it.

cuts.event: The Commons Registration (Glamorgan) Act 1983 validates the Glamorgan common-land registers.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: Parliament validates the Glamorgan common-land registers [EV-0232]. The Act covers common land; VG41 is a village-green registration [EV-0044]. No direct effect on the farmhouse has been found.
cuts.open: Which 1983 step is meant here? If it is the farmhouse registration, see C25 and C27.

cuts.event: BP Properties issues a writ for possession against her son, the occupier.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The son is sued as occupier [EV-0073] [EV-0088]. The family is now the defendant.

cuts.event: High Court trial in Cardiff; Hollis J gives judgment for BP.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: Judgment for BP: Frederick's possession held not adverse, and the 1974 letters held to make Mary a licensee, so the limitation defence under the 1939 and 1980 Acts failed [EV-0074] [EV-0075].

cuts.event: The farmhouse title is merged into the farm title (application, WA231076 item 14) while the appeal is pending.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The farmhouse title is merged into the farm title, WA231076 item 14, while the appeal is pending [EV-0078].
cuts.open: What class of title was granted in 1983? If possessory, the rules from 1 Jan 1987 on upgrading during an open adverse claim would apply. The register would answer it.

cuts.event: Court of Appeal: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 dismisses the appeal. Possession in six weeks; leave to appeal to the House of Lords refused.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: The appeal is dismissed; possession in six weeks; leave to appeal to the House of Lords refused [EV-0080]. The court accepted adverse possession by Frederick and Mary from 1955 and held that the 1962 order and the 1974 letters defeated it.

cuts.event: Petition for leave to appeal to the House of Lords.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: A petition for leave to appeal to the House of Lords is lodged [EV-0076]. The outcome papers are not yet held.
cuts.open: What became of the petition? The House of Lords Journal would answer it.

cuts.event: Application to the European Commission of Human Rights (14464/88), later declared inadmissible.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: Application 14464/88 to the European Commission of Human Rights is declared inadmissible, so there is no hearing on the merits [EV-0122].

cuts.event: First eviction attempt; BP's spokesman explains the case to the press.
cuts.label: Record (press)
cuts.changed: The first eviction attempt is reported [EV-0089] [EV-0090] [EV-0092]; BP's spokesman sets out BP's account of the case [EV-0088]. The word "squatters" is a label others applied to the family.

cuts.event: Estates Gazette: "BP signal Welsh sales".
cuts.label: Record (press)
cuts.changed: The Estates Gazette reports BP planning sales in Wales [EV-0093]. No record yet ties the 1982–83 filings to a sale.
cuts.open: Was the farm part of the 1988 sale? Sale particulars or the Land Registry history would answer it.

cuts.event: Cadw inspects and photographs the house; the listing decision comes in December 1988.
cuts.label: Record
cuts.changed: Cadw inspects and photographs the house in July 1988 [EV-0094] [EV-0095] [EV-0096]; the listing decision is dated December 1988 [EV-0103].
cuts.open: When did Cadw's decision reach BP and the council? The listing file would answer it.

cuts.event: Forced entry and the outbuilding roof removed; the residents are evicted; Mr Buckler is taken from a hospital bed to face an assault charge.
cuts.label: Record (press)
cuts.changed: Forced entry, the outbuilding roof removed and the residents evicted [EV-0098] [EV-0099] [EV-0101]; Mr Buckler is taken from a hospital bed to face an assault charge [EV-0102].
cuts.open: What became of the assault charge? The magistrates' record would answer it.

cuts.event: The final eviction hearing in the Cardiff High Court fails.
cuts.label: Record (press)
cuts.changed: The application at the Cardiff High Court fails [EV-0104] [EV-0105].

cuts.event: The farmhouse is demolished ("Tears flow as 800 year-old farm house is razed at last").
cuts.label: Record (press, SMR)
cuts.changed: The farmhouse is demolished [EV-0106] [EV-0107]. The Sites and Monuments Record later enters "building destroyed by owners" [EV-0108].

epilogue.event: Vale councillors authorise legal action against BP Properties over the demolition.
Sites and Monuments Record PRN 02038s: "building destroyed by owners".
Outline planning permission for houses at Great House Farm (89/01396/OUT).
Reserved matters approved and 20 houses built.

decided: Jul 1955: possession of the whole farm except the farmhouse and garden, under a High Court order [EV-0080] (the order itself is not yet located). See C10.
11 Dec 1962: possession of the farmhouse and garden, Cardiff County Court [EV-0041]. See C13.
Sep 1974: leave to execute the 1962 order [EV-0041]. See C19.
Jul 1986: judgment for BP; Frederick's possession not adverse; Mary a licensee from the 31 Oct 1974 letters [EV-0074] [EV-0075]. See C30.

31 Jul 1987: appeal dismissed; the 1962 order stopped the clock before 12 years; from the 1974 letters possession was no longer adverse; adverse possession from 1955 accepted; leave to appeal to the House of Lords refused [EV-0080]. See C32.
1988: the human-rights application declared inadmissible [EV-0122], and the final eviction hearing of 6 Dec 1988 failed [EV-0104]. See C34 and C39.
undecided: The 3 Jul 1974 plea that BP's claim was barred by adverse possession: adjourned part-heard and, in the Court of Appeal's words, "has never been finally heard" [EV-0049] [EV-0080]. See C18.
No court decision on the record determines who owned the farmhouse as a question of title; the 1986 and 1987 judgments decided possession and limitation [EV-0075] [EV-0080].

No record of compensation for the demolition, and no finding against any party for it, has been located. The outcome of the Vale councillors' 1989 decision to take legal action [EV-0117] is not yet located.
The House of Lords outcome papers are not yet held [EV-0076]. See C33.
against: The Court of Appeal held that the 1962 order stopped the 12-year period before it ran, and that from the 1974 letters Mary's possession was no longer adverse [EV-0080]. These holdings stand unless set aside.
The judgment records rent arrears in the 1930s and 1940s and a last payment in 1953 [EV-0080], against the family's account of rent ending in 1928 [EV-0016].
The trial judge found that Frederick had no intention to possess as owner, relying on the March 1965 offer [EV-0080]. See C12.
BP did not depend on the 1983 registration to sue: the 1984 action succeeded on the 1974 letters [EV-0073] [EV-0080].
No record yet shows BP knew of Mary's final illness, or that the 1983 filing was timed to it.
open: What does the 1974 Cardiff County Court file show was pleaded and left undecided? The HMCTS reply due 2 Nov 2026 would show it [EV-0049].

What did BP and its solicitors tell the Land Registry in 1983 about who lived in the house? The application papers and the 8 Apr, 12 Apr and 12 May 1983 letters (Registry reply due 28 Oct 2026) would show it [EV-0069] [EV-0070].
Did Mary or her solicitors reject the licence after 31 Oct 1974 in writing? A letter doing so would meet the point the Court of Appeal identified [EV-0080].
Was the farmhouse parcel inside the 1938 Bute–Western Ground Rents conveyance and plan [EV-0019] [EV-0023]?
Each "Open question" line in the entries above is a further ingredient still missing.

labels_note: Record = read in a court judgment, registry, archive, legislation or contemporaneous press. Family testimony = the family's own account. Not yet confirmed = no source located yet. Open question = what the record does not yet answer, and what would answer it.
lede: Each entry gives a date, what happened, what it changed in law or in fact, and the evidence pages it rests on. "Depends on" and "Enabled" link each entry to the earlier entries it built on and the later ones that built on it. Open both ends of a link to check it.

periods.0: 1870s–1939: the family at Great House Farm

theories.intro: Competing theories that could account for the entries above, ordered from most to least plausible given all the evidence held today: how much of the record each accounts for, and how much stands against it. Each is a theory, not a finding. The courts' view is included and ranked like the others.

items.title: The courts' view: possession was lawfully recovered and the paper title was never extinguished
items.theory: The family held as tenants until the 1955 notice to quit, then as adverse possessors; the 1962 order stopped the 12-year period before it ran, and the 31 Oct 1974 letters made Mary's later possession a licence, so the paper title running from Bute through the 1938 conveyance to BP was never extinguished and possession was recovered lawfully.
items.for: The 1916 tenancy of "the whole of the farm" [EV-0014]; the 1953 rent payment under a judgment [EV-0080]; the 1962 possession order [EV-0041]; the 1974 letters [EV-0050]; the High Court judgment [EV-0075] and the Court of Appeal [EV-0080]. These holdings bind unless set aside.
items.against: The 1974 adverse-possession plea "has never been finally heard" [EV-0049]; the family's account of rent ending in 1928 [EV-0016]; the 1939 plan shows only the fields [EV-0023]; whether the 1938 conveyance included the farmhouse parcel has not been read [EV-0019].
items.test: Confirmed by a 1938 conveyance plan that includes the farmhouse parcel and by the absence of any written rejection of the 1974 licence. Refuted by a plan that leaves the farmhouse out, or a letter rejecting the licence after 31 Oct 1974.

items.title: Lawful steps, sequenced against the limitation clock
items.theory: Each step was lawful on its own, but together they kept the family's possession from ever running its 12 years, without the ownership plea being decided: the 1962 order, its revival about 12 weeks before the period from it ended, the licence letters, and the 1983 registration while Mary was alive.
items.for: Leave to execute in Sep 1974 against an 11 Dec 1974 expiry [EV-0041] [EV-0080]; the letters of 31 Oct 1974 [EV-0050]; the undecided 1974 plea [EV-0049]; the 1983 application made in her lifetime [EV-0066]; BP's spokesman in 1988 on waiting until her death [EV-0088].
items.against: Waiting for her death is also what the 1974 letters promised [EV-0050]; the 1982 field registration was compulsory [EV-0265]; BP's 1984 action succeeded on the 1974 letters, not on the 1983 registration [EV-0080]; no record yet shows BP knew of her final illness.
items.test: Confirmed or refuted by the 1974 Cardiff County Court file (HMCTS reply due 2 Nov 2026) [EV-0049] and BP's own files on the 1974 and 1983 steps.

items.title: The farmhouse parcel stood outside the paper chain
items.theory: Parcel A, the house parcel, was never conveyed in the Bute → Western Ground Rents chain, so the possession cases started from a paper title that did not cover the house.
items.for: The 1939 agreement plan highlights the fields only [EV-0023]; the family's account of the house standing apart [EV-0016]; the separate 1983 registration of the farmhouse [EV-0066].
items.against: The 1916 tenancy covers "the whole of the farm" with plan [EV-0014]; the courts took the paper title to the farm as their starting point [EV-0080]; the 1938 conveyance and its plan have not yet been read [EV-0019].
items.test: Settled either way by the 1938 Bute–Western Ground Rents conveyance and plan, and the 1905 Bute conveyance.

items.title: The 1983 registration misdescribed the occupation
items.theory: BP's 1983 application for the farmhouse, made while Mary lived there and examined after her death, did not tell the Registry the true position of the occupier.
items.for: The application date and her death in the weeks after it [EV-0066] [EV-0067]; the 8 Apr, 12 Apr and 12 May 1983 letters exist [EV-0069] [EV-0070] [EV-0071]; the house title was merged into the farm title while the appeal was pending [EV-0078].
items.against: What the letters say is not yet known; registration times in 1982–83 were ordinary; the 1984 action did not depend on the registration [EV-0080].
items.test: Confirmed or refuted by the Land Registry's 1983 application papers and letters (reply due 28 Oct 2026).

items.title: A 1988 sale drove the clearance
items.theory: The site had become an asset for sale in 1988, and the clearance served that sale.
items.for: "BP signal Welsh sales", Estates Gazette, 9 Jul 1988 [EV-0093]; the 1975 deed reserved road and sewer rights "to serve any development" [EV-0052]; houses followed from 1990 [EV-0124].
items.against: No record ties the farm to the 1988 sale; the land was still being sold off by BP Properties in 1989 and 1993; the 1986 charge to Intercontinental was over a London office, not Llandough.
items.test: Sale particulars for 1988–93, or the Land Registry history of WA231076.
